reader.requirement: At --std 85 the alphabet named by PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE orders every nonnumeric (alphabetic, alphanumeric, numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited, group) SORT and MERGE key, whatever the input/output form (USING/GIVING or procedures) and in contained programs, unless the statement's own COLLATING SEQUENCE phrase names an alphabet, which then wins; numeric keys are compared algebraically and are untouched.

edition-consulted.switches: the 2002 alphabet-name-2 / FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL forms of the SORT/MERGE phrase (construct sort-collating-national-2002, COBOL0872): refused at 85, admitted at 2023; the single alphabet-name-1 form 1985 prints is not gated
the 2002 national surface of PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (program-collating-national-2002): refused at 85; the 1985 single-name form passes
nothing: the EditionContext is only the diagnostic sink for a repeated FOR phrase

reader.edition-search: grep -i collating over Validation/ and WiseOwl.Cobol.Editions/ (ConstructRegistry.g.cs rows sort-collating-national-2002, program-collating-national-2002); read SortBinder.SortBindCollating and SpecialNamesBinder.ResolveProgramCollating for DialectLevel/CobolVersion tests: none; the PCS-or-phrase precedence and the key-class selection (CollatingSelection.Of, SortKeyColumns.SequenceFor) are edition-neutral.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the 1985 forms; yes: the later editions' alphabet-name-2 / FOR phrases (national keys) are refused at 85 with COBOL0872, which the 1985 format requires since it prints only alphabet-name-1.

reader.notes: The program collating sequence is bound once into Configuration.Collating and SortBindCollating takes it unless the statement names its own alphabet; the runtime applies the sequence only to alphanumeric-class keys, so numeric keys stay algebraic and numeric-edited keys collate. Class a (variable length) does not apply to the rule beyond the fixed SD probed; the diagnostics at 85 still cite §2023 clause numbers, a message-text matter outside this rule.
